source_text: Totum denique, quod egerat, enodavit dicens: Sicut enim per inoboedientiam unius hominis peccatores constituti sunt multi, ita et per unius oboedientiam iusti constituentur multi [n199] , ut, sicut nemo praemia virtutis meretur, nisi qui ad ea post incarnationem tamen Christi sanctitatis eius imitatione contenderit, ita in Adam praevaricator nemo teneatur, nisi qui in transgressione legis, qua peccati est facta cognitio, primi hominis imitatione deliquerit.
pass_a_gloss: Finally he unknotted the whole which he had done, saying: For as through the disobedience of one human being many were constituted sinners, so also through the obedience of one many will be constituted just, so that, as no one merits the prizes of virtue except he who after the incarnation nevertheless of Christ has contended toward them by imitation of his holiness, so in Adam no one is held a transgressor except he who in a transgression of the law, by which knowledge of sin was made, has offended by imitation of the first human being.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: He untangled the whole argument by saying: ‘For just as through one man’ (Romans 3:20)s disobedience many were made sinners, so through one man’s obedience many will be made righteous’ (Romans 5:19). Thus, just as no one earns virtue’s rewards unless, after Christ’s incarnation, he strives toward them by imitating Christ’s holiness, so no one is held as a transgressor in Adam unless he has sinned in imitation of the first man, transgressing the law through which knowledge of sin came (allusion to Romans 3:20).

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Adam's act of crossing the command; Julian's example of sin, not a transmitted nature.
